title: Microsoft Teams: app centric management of app access in the Teams admin center for DoD
summary: Hold: the briefing calls the migration and arrival behaviour unstated even though its cited Learn page describes automatic migration and the mapping of existing settings, without excluding DoD. The per-app control and PowerShell call are documented, but the default and action guidance need correction.

claims.where: What's changing, first paragraph; front matter: changes
claims.claim: The roadmap describes evolving permission policies and migrating existing customers' policies to maintain app availability.
claims.quote: This feature evolves the existing app permission policies and provides admins with the ability to manage access to the app individually. The app permission policies for existing customers are migrated to maintain existing app availability in the tenant.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Each app carries its own access definition as an assigned list of users and groups.
claims.quote: Each app contains its access definition using a list of users and groups that you assign to it.

claims.claim: Learn names the per-app options Everyone, Specific users or groups, and No one.
claims.quote:
| `Everyone` | Available to all org users, new users, and guests. |
| `Specific users or groups` | Only the users and groups that you select can use the app.
| `No one` | Not available to any user

claims.claim: The previous access model used the org-wide third-party setting, app allow/block status and user permission policy.
claims.quote:
Previously, when using permission policies, you determined access to apps using the following three settings:
- Org-wide app setting for third-party apps
- App status
- Permission policy

claims.claim: After switching, administrators cannot access, edit or use permission policies.
claims.quote: After you switch to this feature, you can't access, edit, or use permission policies.

claims.claim: The migration cannot be reverted.
claims.quote: Once your organization migrates, you can't revert the migration.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters, second paragraph; Open questions
claims.claim: The migration's arrival behaviour is unknown because Microsoft has not said whether DoD tenants migrate automatically.
claims.quote:
Starting from April 2025, your tenant is automatically migrated to app centric management.
For existing organizations, old settings are mapped to new access settings.
claims.fix: Set defaultState to on. Replace the sentence beginning 'Microsoft has not stated what a DoD tenant sees on arrival' with 'Learn describes automatic migration to app centric management and maps existing organisations' old settings to new access settings; it does not publish a DoD-specific rollout window.' In the first Open questions bullet retain the DoD rollout-window question but remove 'and will the migration be automatic?'. Remove the second Open questions bullet questioning whether the documented migration rules apply: the general documentation does not exclude DoD. Do not apply Learn's general April 2025 date as a DoD rollout date; retain this item's November CY2026 roadmap target.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Learn's limitations section says an app allowed globally but blocked by a custom policy becomes available to all tenant users during automatic migration, except in EDU.
claims.quote: There's no change of app permissions during the migration, except where an app is allowed in the global policy but blocked in the custom app permission policy. Here, the app is available to all users of the tenant, except for EDU customers, for whom it will be available to none.

claims.claim: In the documented EDU exception, that app becomes available to none.
claims.quote: except for EDU customers, for whom it will be available to none.

claims.claim: Everyone includes current organisation users, new users and guests.
claims.quote: `Everyone` | Available to all org users, new users, and guests.

claims.claim: Specific users or groups excludes guests even when assigned.
claims.quote: Guests can't use the app if this option is selected and even if guests are assigned to the app.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Automatic migration creates one security group per custom app permission policy.
claims.quote: During the auto migration, one security group is created for each custom app permission policy.

claims.claim: Users assigned to each former policy are added to its corresponding group.
claims.quote: All users currently assigned to an app permission policy are then added to the corresponding security group for that policy.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: group membership
claims.claim: The created groups are assigned to apps allowed by their policies, and managing those groups changes app assignments.
claims.quote: These groups are assigned to each app they're allowed in their respective policy, maintaining their app access. Administrators manage these groups like any others to customize the app centric management assignments

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; controls[1].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Org-wide settings do not override individually saved Specific users or groups, Everyone or No one availability.
claims.quote:
The Org-wide app settings don’t apply to:
- All apps that have user assignment set to Specific users and groups and saved by you.
- All apps that were assigned to Everyone or to No one and saved individually.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; controls[1].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Org-wide app settings do not override blocked apps.
claims.quote:
The Org-wide app settings don’t apply to:
- Any blocked apps.
